notes:
19 components, 9 nets. The sheet is a regular 5-column ladder: three horizontal rails (top y~342, middle y~484, bottom y~650) crossed by five vertical columns (x~97, 271, 446, 635, 785). Each column carries one two-terminal part between the top and middle rails and another between the middle and bottom rails; six further parts are inserted inside the rails themselves, and a 2k resistor hangs off the right end of the middle rail down to a second ground.

JUDGEMENT CALLS
S13 (99,478), S14 (784,483), S15 (272,485), S16 (446,484), S17 (635,486) - the five places where a column crosses the middle rail, the only genuine junction-vs-crossing decisions on this sheet. I read all five as JUNCTIONS. Evidence: (a) I dumped the raw pixels at all five with inkmap - in every one the vertical runs straight through the horizontal with no arc, no lateral jog beyond 3-5 px of pen drift, and no gap; there is not a single hop anywhere on this drawing, so the drafter's 'not connected' marker is simply absent; (b) the ink prior says a plain crossing in this dataset is a real junction; (c) structurally this is a ladder - on the top rail every column meets the rail as an unambiguous T (S4, S5, S3, plus corners at x~97 and x~785) and on the bottom rail likewise (S24, S25, S26, plus corners), so the middle rail crossings are the shared mid-node of each column pair and reading them as crossings would make the layout inconsistent with itself. The alternative reading (crossing at S14/S16/S17, which have dot scores of only 1.6 against 2.5/2.7 at S13/S15) is electrically sane too - it would peel {Diode#5 bottom, Zener#12 top}, {Zener#4 bottom, Diode#11 top} and {Diode#6 bottom, Diode#14 top} off as three isolated 2-terminal nets and shorten the middle rail to three segments - but the dot-score spread is not real evidence here: the plain T-junctions on this sheet score 1.0-1.8 as well (S5=1.0, S24=1.1, S26=1.5, S4=1.8), so this drafter does not dot his junctions at all and the 2.5/2.7 readings at S13/S15 are just extra stroke overlap where the column kinks sideways by a few pixels.
S3 (626,346), S4 (271,347), S5 (444,350), S24 (289,643), S25 (459,651), S26 (630,652) - plain T's where a diode lead ends on a rail that runs straight through. Junction, each confirmed in its own crop. S3 only became load-bearing after the port fix on #4, so it is recorded explicitly.
All other sites are handwriting on wire ink and were left alone: S8/S9 ('15 uF'), S10/S11 ('8V 1kHz'), S19/S22 ('9 uF'), S23 ('2 k ohm'), S28 ('1 uH').

#1 Capacitor 15 uF: t1 was on p2 @ (518,363), the top of the '1' in '15 uF'. Moved to p1 @ (518,346), the real left-plate lead on the top rail. (Was net n4 alone.)
#2 V-AC 8 V: t1 was on p2 @ (126,414), a stroke of the 'kHz' label. Moved to p1 @ (96,364), the real top lead, which runs up to y~342 and right into the inductor. (Was net n5 alone; it also left n1 with a single terminal.)
#4 Zener 5 V: t0 was on p2 @ (595,372), the 'F' of the '15 uF' label. Moved to p1 @ (625,372), the real top lead dropping from the top rail at S3. (Was net n6 alone.)
#8 Capacitor 9 uF: t1 was on p2 @ (381,506), the 'u' of the '9 uF' label. Moved to p1 @ (410,482), the real right-plate lead on the middle rail. (Was net n9 alone.)
After these four fixes every one-terminal-net warning is gone and the netlist closes: 36 terminals over 9 nets, ERC clean.

CLASSES
All 19 accepted. I looked hard at the four parts labelled Diode that sit next to parts labelled Zener Diode (#6, #11, #13, #14) at 10x: #3, #4 and #12 carry the long diagonal Z-hooks on both ends of the cathode bar (the right hook on #3 runs a full 20 px up-right), whereas #6, #11, #13 and #14 have plain bars with at most a 4-5 px pen tail on one end. The distinction is consistent, so the COCO labels stand. #10 is a circle with a plain up arrow and the label '3 A' with no frequency, consistent with I-DC; #2 is a circle with a sine and '8V 1kHz', consistent with V-AC. GND #7 is drawn rotated 90 degrees (hatch bars vertical, lead leaving to the right) but is unmistakably a ground. No re-classification needed.

OTHER
The remaining unused port candidate on #0 (177,324) is the '5' of '5 uH' and on #15 (920,619) is the '2' of '2 k ohm'; neither is a lead and the tracer already ignored them. 14 gap bridges, none affecting the netlist, none dropped. Nothing left unresolved.
